This executive order by Governor Nikki Haley declares that a State of Emergency exists in South Carolina. Accordingly, I direct the South Carolina Emergency Operations Plan be placed into effect and require state agencies to support the responsibilities and tasks therein.  She further orders the utilization of the South Carolina National
Guard's personnel with appropriate equipment, at the discretion of the Adjutant General
Executive Order 2014-11 and in coordination with the South Carolina Emergency Management Division, to take necessary and prudent actions to assist the citizens of this state. — Severe storms--South Carolina
This executive order by Governor Nikki Haley declare that a State of Emergency exists in South Carolina due to severe winter weather between January 28, 2014 and January 30, 2014.
This executive order by Governor Mark Sanford declares a state of emergency due to the expected snow.
This executive order by Governor Mark Sanford declares a state of emergency exists in Horry County due to wildfires.
This executive order by Governor Mark Sanford declares a state of emergency due to weather conditions of tornadoes and hail.

This executive order by Governor Mark Sanford declares a state of emergency due to the possible effects of Tropical Storm Gaston and directs that the South Carolina Emergency Operations Plan be placed into effect.

This executive order by Governor Mark Sanford declares a state of emergency and directs that the South Carolina Emergency Operations Plan be placed into effect due to the possible dangers of Hurricane Charley.
This executive order by Governor Mark Sanford declares a state of emergency for Greenville County due to severe flooding.
This executive order by Governor Mark Sanford declares a state of emergency due to expected severe winter weather and orders the South Carolina National Guard be placed on standby status.

This executive order by Governor Mark Sanford declares a state of emergency for the purpose of suspending federal regulations limiting the hours operators of commercial vehicles may drive, in order to ensure uninterrupted supply of fuel. — Winter storms--South Carolina
This executive order by Governor Mark Sanford declares a state of emergency due to the winter weather and directs that the South Carolina Emergency Operations Plan be placed in effect.

This executive order by Governor Jim Hodges declares a state of emergency due to inclement weather. The need to continue the uninterrupted supply of food and fuel justifies an exemption for the federal regulations on how long commercial vehicles may drive. — Winter storms--South Carolina
This executive order by Governor Jim Hodges declares a state of emergency due to incoming winter storms and directs that the South Carolina Emergency Operation Plans be placed in effect.

This executive order by Governor Jim Hodges declares a state of emergency due to tornadoes and significant flooding in the following counties: Clarendon, Georgetown, Berkeley, Calhoun, Charleston, Florence, Horry, Marion, Orangeburg, Sumter, and Williamsburg.
This executive order by Governor Jim Hodges declares a state of emergency for Horry County due to wildfires.
This executive order by Governor Jim Hodges declares a state of emergency due to the large amounts of snow and ice, and orders the South Carolina National Guard to take appropriate action.
This executive order by Governor Jim Hodges declares a state of emergency in Horry County due to wildfires.

This executive order by Governor Jim Hodges declares a State of Emergency due to the inclement weather and the need to continue the uninterrupted supply of fuel oil, kerosene, and propane. For these reasons, the Governor authorizes drivers of commercial vehicles to operate for longer hours than certain Federal Motor Carrier Safety regulations normally allow. — Winter storms--South Carolina

This executive order by Governor Jim Hodges declares a State of Emergency due to the cold weather and the need to continue the uninterrupted supply of fuel oil, kerosene, and propane, which justifies an exemption from Part 395.3(b) of Title 49 of the Code of Federal Regulations (limits on the hours operators of commercial vehicles may drive).

This executive order by Governor Jim Hodges declares a state of emergency due to incoming winter storms and directs that the South Carolina National Guard will be place on standby status and will take all reasonable and necessary actions to prepare for and respond to the hazards of this severe winter weather at the discretion of the Adjutant General and as determined necessary by the South Carolina Emergency Preparedness Division.

This executive order by Governor Jim Hodges declares a State of Emergency due to the cold weather and the need to continue the uninterrupted supply of Liquefied Petroleum Gas and allows for the suspension of Part 395 (drivers' hours of service) of Title 49 of the Code of Federal Regulations for 30 days or until the emergency conditions cease to exist.

This executive order by Governor Jim Hodges declares a State of Emergency due to the cold weather and the need to continue the uninterrupted supply of Liquefied Petroleum Gas (propane) and allows for an exemption from Parts 390 of Title 49 of the Code of Federal Regulations which limits the hours operators of commercial vehicles may drive.
This executive order by Governor James H. Hodges declares a state of emergency in Georgetown, Horry, and Marion counties due to flooding caused by Hurricane Floyd.
